sentences.text: If you dig a hole in the yard and fill it with water, you have a pool.
But the water soaks into the soil and leaks away.
Within an hour, the hole is empty bare mud.
But now the wet walls slump in, since a cubic yard of soil can weigh about 3,000 pounds.
So you pour a concrete floor and walls to hold back the water and soil.
So you fill the shell with 20,000 gallons, which weigh around 83 tons.
But now the water goes stale, so a pipe from the bottom carries it to a pump.
Then a filter tank catches the dirt, and a second pipe sends clean water back.
This is a swimming pool.
The pump, filter and pipes together are the circulation system.
The pump pulls water from the bottom, the filter strains out dirt, and clean water flows back.
A typical pump pushes the pool's whole volume through the filter about once every 8 hours.
The clock ticks through 8 hours, and many pools run 8 to 10 hours a day.
But now the filter cannot stop living algae, so in the sun the water turns green.
Then a storm blows leaves and mud in, and the water gets murkier.
So you add chlorine, and the water clears.
And the blue color is not paint on the pool.
Water itself absorbs red light and sends blue back, so it looks blue.
Add a fence, bushes and young trees around the pool.
Congratulations, you have built a swimming pool.
